title: Pankaj Tripathi Just Produced His First Show — and It Puts Your Family on the Therapist's Couch
excerpt: Perfect Family on SonyLIV is messy, funny, uncomfortably real, and features Gulshan Devaiah and Manoj Pahwa at their finest
body:
The Karkarias look like any upper-middle-class Indian family you've ever met — loud dinners, strong opinions, a patriarch who thinks raising his voice counts as communication, a matriarch who weaponises silence with surgical precision. They throw parties, they squabble about investments, they love each other in that specific, suffocating way that makes you want to scream and also never leave home.

<youtube></youtube>

Then the youngest daughter has a breakdown at school. And suddenly, the cracks in the Karkaria foundation aren't just visible — they're load-bearing.

**Perfect Family**, which began streaming on **SonyLIV** on **June 26**, is one of the most quietly devastating things to arrive on Indian OTT this year. It is also, somehow, one of the funniest. Created by **Palak Bhambri** and directed by **Sachin Pathak**, the eight-episode series follows a dysfunctional family forced into therapy after their daughter's meltdown signals something much deeper than academic stress. What unfolds is equal parts cringe comedy and emotional reckoning — a family realising that the very things they've never said out loud are the things destroying them.



> **"*The Indian Express* called it "beautifully relatable" and gave it 3.5 out of 5."**


The casting alone makes this essential viewing. **Manoj Pahwa** plays Somnath Karkaria, the family's volcanic centre — aggressive, abusive in ways he doesn't recognise, and heartbreakingly funny when he's cornered by a therapist who won't let him deflect. **Seema Pahwa** is Kamla, his wife, who has spent decades absorbing his eruptions and turning them into her own quiet brand of dysfunction. Together, the real-life couple deliver performances so raw they feel less like acting and more like eavesdropping.

> "The beauty of this show lies in its honesty. It doesn't try to give easy answers or perfect characters. It simply holds up a mirror to family dynamics in a very raw and relatable way." — Neha Dhupia

**Gulshan Devaiah** anchors the generational middle as Vishnu, a son desperate to prove his worth in a household that never taught him how to ask for what he needs. **Girija Oak Godbole** is devastating as Neeti — blunt, furious, tired of performing the role of the accommodating daughter-in-law. And **Neha Dhupia**, as therapist Megha, walks the tightrope between professional composure and barely concealed alarm at what she's uncovered. The ensemble is rounded out by **Kaveri Seth** as Pooja and the remarkable **Hirva Trivedi** as Daani, the child whose crisis sets everything in motion.

The show's secret weapon is its structure. Sessions alternate between one-on-ones and different family permutations — the three women together, the two men squaring off, husband and wife confronting decades of unspoken resentment. It's a format that could feel repetitive in lesser hands, but Pathak uses it to peel back layers with surgical precision. Each session reveals something the previous one was hiding.

What makes **Perfect Family** genuinely important — beyond its considerable entertainment value — is its treatment of therapy itself. In a country where mental health is still whispered about, where "seeing someone" carries stigma and family problems are supposed to stay behind closed doors, the show normalises the messy, uncomfortable, occasionally hilarious process of sitting in a room with people you love and telling the truth. It does this without being preachy, which is perhaps its greatest achievement.

*The Indian Express* called it "beautifully relatable" and gave it 3.5 out of 5. *Scroll.in* praised its "home truths about family relationships." *India Today* noted that the series "resists the glossy facade" of typical family drama. The consensus: it's flawed, it occasionally over-explains, but when it lands — and it lands often — it hits somewhere between your ribs.


The show also marks **Pankaj Tripathi's** debut as a producer. That a man who has built his career playing characters from India's margins chose a therapy drama about an outwardly privileged family for his first production says something interesting about where Indian storytelling is heading. The problems aren't always economic. Sometimes the people who look most put-together are the ones falling apart.

## Where to Watch

**Perfect Family** is streaming exclusively on **SonyLIV**. For diaspora viewers, SonyLIV International is available in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and across the Middle East. All eight episodes are available now.

Fair warning: you will recognise your own family in the Karkarias. That's the point. And it stings in the best possible way.
